The test image shows a **stem** cut open longitudinally, revealing:
- Bleached/whitened, dry, fibrous pith interior
- Dark structures inside that look like sclerotia
- Decayed, brown outer stem tissue

This strongly suggests **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (diagnostic: sliced stem showing grayish-black sclerotia). Let me view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.

Excellent match — same Bugwood source (5593844 vs 5593851 in test), same black plastic mulch background, bleached stem with dark sclerotia visible. Now checking 3 more classes to fulfill the 4-class requirement.
Southern_Blight stem doesn't show the dark sclerotia pattern seen in the test. Now checking Alternaria and Bacterial_Wilt.
Alternaria doesn't match — dark external canker, no internal sliced view. Now the 4th class reference.

Bacterial_Wilt shows bacterial ooze streaming from a stem in water — completely different from the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Class | Reference | Match |
|---|---|---|
| Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot | Bugwood_21 (5593844) | **Strong match** — same Bugwood series, black plastic mulch, bleached stem, dark sclerotia inside |
| Southern_Blight | Bugwood_15 | No — sliced stem but no sclerotia, different tissue appearance |
| Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers | Bugwood_4 | No — dark external canker at soil line, uncut stem |
| Bacterial_Wilt | Bugwood_3 | No — bacterial ooze in water diagnostic |

The test image is a longitudinally sliced tomato stem showing:
- Bleached/whitened, dry pith interior
- Dark grayish-black structures inside = sclerotia
- Black plastic mulch background (matches the Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot Bugwood reference exactly)

This perfectly matches the KB description: *"Hard, grayish-black sclerotia about the size of a plump grain of rice embedded within the stem tissue; positive identification achieved by slicing the diseased stem longitudinally."*
